title: Parenthood + Parent Layer
stage: Parenthood; the Parent Layer that closes the generational loop

myths.myth: Once you're parents, the relationship takes a back seat forever.
myths.truth: Nurturing the partnership is part of a healthy home.
myths.explanation: Kids benefit from parents who are okay too.

myths.myth: Good parents lose themselves entirely in the kids.
myths.truth: You can be a great parent and still a whole person.
myths.explanation: Modelling a full life teaches kids to have one.

myths.myth: Wanting time alone — or together, without kids — is selfish.
myths.truth: Rest and connection refill the tank.
myths.explanation: You can't pour from empty.

myths.myth: Intimacy fading after kids is just how it is.
myths.truth: It changes, and can be rebuilt with communication.
myths.explanation: Talking beats drifting.

myths.myth: Mums are the 'real' parent; dads just 'babysit'.
myths.truth: Both parents can fully parent.
myths.explanation: A father raising his own kids isn't babysitting.

myths.myth: Fathers aren't meant to do nappies or night feeds.
myths.truth: Caregiving is learned by doing — by anyone.
myths.explanation: Hands-on dads raise more secure kids.

myths.myth: One 'default parent' carrying everything is normal.
myths.truth: Sharing the load — and the mental load — is the goal.
myths.explanation: One burnt-out parent helps no one.

myths.myth: Paternity leave is basically a holiday.
myths.truth: It's bonding and care work that matters.
myths.explanation: Early involvement shapes lifelong roles.

myths.myth: A good parent never feels overwhelmed.
myths.truth: Overwhelm is normal; support helps.
myths.explanation: Struggling doesn't mean failing.

myths.myth: Asking for help with your kids means you're inadequate.
myths.truth: It takes a village — using it is wise.
myths.explanation: No one parents well entirely alone.

myths.myth: Postnatal depression is just 'baby blues' to push through.
myths.truth: It's real, common and treatable.
myths.explanation: Getting help protects you and the baby.

myths.myth: Your needs come dead last now — forever.
myths.truth: Your wellbeing is part of your kids' wellbeing.
myths.explanation: Secure parents raise secure kids.

myths.myth: 'The talk' is one big conversation at puberty.
myths.truth: It's many small, age-appropriate conversations over years.
myths.explanation: Little and often beats one awkward lecture.

myths.myth: Teaching kids the real names for body parts is inappropriate.
myths.truth: Correct names actually keep kids safer.
myths.explanation: Clear language helps them report harm.

myths.myth: Talking about bodies and consent makes kids grow up too fast.
myths.truth: Age-appropriate information protects — it doesn't corrupt.
myths.explanation: Silence just leaves them to the internet.

myths.myth: If you don't bring it up, they won't think about it.
myths.truth: They'll learn somewhere — better from you.
myths.explanation: You'd rather be the trusted source.

myths.myth: 'I was hit and I turned out fine.'
myths.truth: We can keep the love and drop the harm.
myths.explanation: Better tools exist than fear.

myths.myth: Discipline means punishment.
myths.truth: Discipline means teaching — with limits and warmth.
myths.explanation: Connection works better than control.

myths.myth: Apologising to your kids undermines your authority.
myths.truth: Repair models accountability.
myths.explanation: Kids learn to say sorry by seeing it done.

myths.myth: You're doomed to parent the way you were parented.
myths.truth: Patterns can be noticed and changed.
myths.explanation: Awareness is what breaks the cycle.

myths.myth: A gender-diverse child is a phase to correct.
myths.truth: Supporting your child's identity keeps them safe and loved.
myths.explanation: Acceptance dramatically lowers their risk of harm.

myths.myth: Talking about gender 'makes' kids queer or trans.
myths.truth: It doesn't; it just makes home safe.
myths.explanation: Kids do best when they're seen.

myths.myth: Love means 'fixing' them to fit in.
myths.truth: Love means protecting them as they are.
myths.explanation: Belonging at home is protective.

myths.myth: There's nothing you can do but worry.
myths.truth: Affirming parents are the single biggest protective factor.
myths.explanation: Your support changes outcomes.

myths.myth: Autism or ADHD is bad parenting or 'too much screen time'.
myths.truth: It's a difference in how a brain works.
myths.explanation: Blame helps no one; understanding does.

myths.myth: They'll 'grow out of it' if you're strict enough.
myths.truth: Support and accommodation help them thrive.
myths.explanation: Fit the environment to the child, not the reverse.

myths.myth: A diagnosis is just a label that limits them.
myths.truth: It's a key to the right support.
myths.explanation: Understanding unlocks help.

myths.myth: Neurodiverse kids can't succeed.
myths.truth: With support they thrive in their own way.
myths.explanation: Different isn't less.

myths.myth: Addiction is just a lack of willpower.
myths.truth: It's a health issue, not a moral failing.
myths.explanation: Shame fuels it; support heals it.

myths.myth: If you talk about substances, you encourage them.
myths.truth: Honest, early conversations reduce risk.
myths.explanation: Information beats mystery.

myths.myth: Screen or phone overuse isn't a real concern.
myths.truth: Habits can become compulsive; balance matters.
myths.explanation: Model and guide — don't just police.

myths.myth: A struggling kid just needs tougher punishment.
myths.truth: Connection and professional help work better.
myths.explanation: Punishment drives it underground.

myths.myth: 'Stranger danger' is the main risk.
myths.truth: Most harm comes from known adults.
myths.explanation: Teach kids about behaviour, not just strangers.

myths.myth: If my kid were in trouble, I'd just know.
myths.truth: Kids hide what they fear they'll be blamed for.
myths.explanation: An open, no-blame door is what keeps them talking.

myths.myth: Keeping secrets is part of family loyalty.
myths.truth: 'No secrets that make you uncomfortable' keeps kids safe.
myths.explanation: Safe adults don't ask for silence.

myths.myth: Teaching consent and safety is the school's job.
myths.truth: You're the first and most important safe adult.
myths.explanation: This is exactly where the loop begins again.

capstone.name: Raising the Next Generation
capstone.landing: Sticker-book spread of every Ch.8 sticker earned; erased parenting myths glowing as ghosts under their truths; a loop arrow that lights up and curves back to Chapter 1, where a new small Lensy waits with a child at the start of the bright corridor. The player, now the trusted adult, hands over the lens. The only capstone that points to a beginning, not just a look back.

canvasFeel: Adult/dark, wry-but-kind but the gentlest of the adult chapters — parenting is hard and the tone never scolds. g64-g69 are the Parent Layer the DD499 report called for, equipping the parent to be the child's primary trusted source. Positive-parenting and evidence-based throughout (affirming-parenting g66, neurodiversity g67, addiction-as-health g68 follow current clinical consensus). The c8 capstone briefly brightens — a sunrise toward Chapter 1 — closing the generational loop the whole product is built around. Sensitive nodes (g65, g68, g69) surface real resources (Childline 1098, counselling).
